thesis: Preserving the present supported probability of a fixed proposition does not necessarily preserve accuracy after further evidence arrives. A source distinction can affect the interpretation of that evidence while leaving the present probability unchanged. Consequently, perfect fit to surviving evidence does not exhaust the assessment of a retention policy, provided foreseeable, costless improvements in expected credal accuracy count in favor of inquiry methods. This is a conditional claim about policy assessment, not a demand to disregard surviving evidence or a refutation of time-slice rationality.
claimed_contribution: A controlled sensor example combines an unchanged present credence, a fixed proposition, a known future inspection, and faultless evidence-relative probabilities under both retention policies. Sections 3–5 use established mathematics to distinguish information preservation from correct updating and to isolate a limitation of an explanation based exclusively on evidential fit. The manuscript expressly disclaims a new information-loss theorem, a new sufficiency theorem, and established priority for its combination of conditions.

findings.manuscript_location: §3, “Why the information loss survives faultless updating”: “The normative and representational antecedents are close”; E[(r-X)^2] - E[(q-X)^2] = E[(q-r)^2]. Also §2, “A label with delayed value for one question”: “Immediately after erasure, the credence in p remains 0.9.”
findings.claim: The literature discussion omits older, directly relevant treatments of complementary signals and forecast refinement.
findings.analysis: Börgers, Hernando-Veciana, and Krähmer give examples involving an otherwise useless decoding key and information about a forecaster’s qualifications. Chen and Waggoner provide a formal binary example in which either signal alone leaves the target probability unchanged, while their combination resolves it. Bröcker’s proper-score decomposition directly covers the expected-loss difference between appropriately related reliable forecasts. These are substantive predecessors to the mechanism, not merely similarly titled works. See [complementary-signal examples](https://www.cirje.e.u-tokyo.ac.jp/research/workshops/micro/micropaper10/micro0518.pdf), introduction, Examples 1–2; [Informational Substitutes](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1703.08636), Example 2.2.2 and §5.2; and [forecast refinement](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0806.0813), equations (13)–(15). The omission is a coverage gap. It does not contradict the manuscript’s explicit acknowledgement that the underlying distinction and mathematics are established.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: The informational mechanism and loss identity cannot constitute the novel contribution. The conditional philosophical conclusion survives; the contribution remains the particular example and its explanatory use in distinguishing inquiry quality from evidential fit.
findings.repair_conditions: Include direct discussion of complementary signals and forecast refinement, specifying how the sensor construction and philosophical application differ. Preserve the existing disclaimers about theorem novelty and unestablished priority.

surviving_contribution: What remains is a specific philosophical application of established information comparisons. The sensor construction makes deletion immediately invisible for p, keeps both policies correct about all propositions relative to their respective information, and produces a later squared-loss difference of 0.01 without changing the question. It also separates that difference from classification performance and from misleading communication. Together with the explicit normative premise, this supplies a counterexample to the proposed deletion test. The opened predecessors establish the main ingredients, but I did not locate this exact sensor construction and philosophical treatment in them. That is a limited search result, not proof of priority.
remaining_questions: §3 explicitly says that “priority for its combination of conditions is not established.” Whether the exact combination or sensor example has appeared elsewhere remains unresolved.

§1 introduces a “proposed answer,” and §5 declines to attribute fit-only completeness to Hedden. No independently defended historical proponent of the exact deletion test was established. Its status should remain a reconstructed temptation rather than an attributed doctrine.

§4’s premise that foreseeable accuracy improvement “counts in favor of a retention method” is a substantive normative commitment. The technical predecessors establish informational comparisons; they do not settle whether the resulting reason is fundamentally epistemic or instrumental. The manuscript correctly leaves that question open.
limitations: The complete supplied manuscript, including its bibliography, was read. External sources were inspected at the locations listed below; this report does not claim complete readings of every external work.

All nine bibliography entries were identified, and their materially used passages were accessible in the cited author or repository versions. Publisher versions were not systematically collated against those versions.
The Aevyra page currently displays version 4.0 and 25 September 2026. I verified that displayed identification and its contents, not an independently archived publication history.

For Börgers, Hernando-Veciana, and Krähmer, the April 2010 working paper was opened and read selectively. Attempts to open the later publisher and Durham repository pages failed; substantive comparisons therefore refer to the working paper.

Blackwell’s 1951 and 1953 originals and DeGroot’s 1962 paper were sought, but attempted retrievals did not provide readable texts. They are not counted as read predecessors or used to establish substantive findings.

Several DOI endpoints and an initial PhilPapers PDF request failed. Accessible author texts and primary bibliographic records resolved the manuscript’s citation checks; the failures themselves are not evidence of citation errors.
The search covered several formulations and adjacent literatures but was finite. It cannot establish exhaustive originality or absence of further predecessors.

closest_predecessors.overlap: An otherwise uninformative signal can help interpret another signal; the forecaster-qualification example directly concerns source quality.
closest_predecessors.difference: The working paper studies economic signal comparisons across decision problems, rather than the manuscript’s retention policies with equal present credence.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: The sensor construction isolates delayed value while holding present credence and subsequent evidential fit fixed.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: Introduction, Examples 1–2, printed pp. 1–2 of the opened working paper; compare manuscript §2, “A label with delayed value for one question.”

closest_predecessors.overlap: Example 2.2.2 uses independent fair bits A1 and A2 with E=A1 XOR A2: either bit alone leaves the probability of E unchanged, but both resolve E. Section 5.2 also treats quadratic scoring. This already supplies the essential informational pattern for one fixed target with correct Bayesian responses.
closest_predecessors.difference: The example starts from an uninformative marginal and concerns signal value and acquisition, without the manuscript’s philosophical retention argument.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: The 0.9 sensor example, classification tie, and distinction between policy merit and evidence-relative correctness remain specific applications.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: Example 2.2.2, printed p. 9; Proposition 5.2.1 and following corollary, printed pp. 38–39; compare manuscript §§2–4.

closest_predecessors.overlap: Equations (13)–(15) distinguish reliability from resolution. Applied to the manuscript’s q and r, both forecasts are reliable and E[q|r]=r; the Brier divergence gives the same expected squared-loss gap. This mapping is my application of the source’s result.
closest_predecessors.difference: Forecast reliability alone is weaker than fitting every proposition to retained evidence. Bröcker does not impose the manuscript’s equal initial marginal and scheduled inspection.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: A philosophical use of an established refinement comparison, with a stronger specification of faultless response.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: §§2–3, equations (13)–(15) and footnote 5; compare manuscript §3’s displayed loss identity and §5’s “fit-only completeness.”

closest_predecessors.overlap: Forgetting is already assessed through expected epistemic value, including retention costs and credences conditional on present evidence.
closest_predecessors.difference: The worked examples immediately alter credences when evidence is forgotten; they do not isolate an unchanged marginal whose loss appears only after a disclosure.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: The manuscript supplies a controlled continuation case within Pettigrew’s acknowledged framework.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: “The value of forgetting,” especially Iona’s example, and “An example”; compare manuscript §3, “this is an application, not an objection to it.”

closest_predecessors.evidence_location: §4.1, Proposition 2; §4.3; §6.2; compare manuscript §3’s distinction between reproducing the full-history answer and answering from retained evidence.

citation_audit.manuscript_location: §2, “A label with delayed value for one question”: posterior table; expected losses 0.07 and 0.08; classification correctness 0.9.
citation_audit.evidence: These are model stipulations and derived calculations, not empirical instrument claims requiring external support.
